text: Core systems are up. Barely.
The cache is thin, the tanks are draining, and nobody has told the people what happens next. That would be you.
Asleep, mostly. Those who could still walk are waiting to see if you keep the lights on.
I would start there.
A hub, a handful of scrap, and a grid that will not carry much.
Power first. Everything else wants it.
One crew, one job at a time, in the order you give them. A job we cannot pay for waits, and so does everything behind it.
The radar hums. Somewhere beyond the walls, the wastes wait.
The tanks are filling and the pantry is not shrinking. I had stopped expecting that.
People are starting to notice. They are looking at the walls differently.
A second site, with its own grid and its own stores. We are no longer one fortress, we are a network.
Keep the roads open. They will be asked to carry more than anyone planned.
The array is standing. All it wants now is power and time.
Whatever answers, we should be ready for it.
Carrier detected. We are listening.
Your message crossed the wastes. Others heard it too.
There is a harbour on the far side. It trades with anyone who has something worth trading.
A market, then. We will need goods that are worth more than scrap.
And we will need to decide who we deal with.
Open hands, then. They will remember who paid well.
A wise instinct. Favours are a currency here, and they are not cheap to earn back.
You have been filling orders. Good. Few do.
The foundries run on tool steel and patience. Bring us the first, and we will teach you the second.
We keep the valleys alive, one jar at a time.
If you can keep our shelves stocked, we can keep your people well.
Meridian moves anything, anywhere, on schedule.
Finished goods by the crate, and we will make sure it gets where it is going.
Word has spread. The factions know your name now, and someone has sent plans for something far bigger than a beacon.
A staging platform and a catapult on the outer ring, and a command center at the harbour. Orbit, if we can afford it.
The station is in orbit. Orbital Command is open: storage, links to the Core, and one dropship.
Below, the anomalies are opening ground nobody has seen. It will not stay open.
Higher now. Closer.
The recovery rig found a data fragment. One fragment is not enough to read anything. Gather more and the records can be assembled into a packet.
A Data screen has opened on your terminal. Look for more data sites in the territories.
More. Keep looking.
Something new in the tray: a requisition. Somebody out there wants ordinary goods from us, a set amount by a set time, in full.
It pays better than the convoy and lends us something for a while when we fill it. If we miss one, another comes.
I asked the courier who it was for. He said, people like us, further down the road.
I had not thought there was a further down the road.
The harbour was not the only one listening. There are camps a day out, on the road. People who saw the light and walked toward it.
They have stopped short of the gate. I think they are waiting to see what we are.
We can sponsor one. It draws a basket of goods from the Core every tick, as much as you allow, and never below what you tell the Core to keep back.

choices.label: What do we get for it?

text: No credits. The foundry camps work on our upgrades, the valley people come and take shifts, and the depots carry our goods further. Each gives in proportion to what it has been getting.
Until it can stand alone. Each stage has a drive, a list to be filled in bulk whenever we can spare it. Fill the last one and it is a town, and a trade partner for good.
More lights. We are counting them.
The last drive is filled. The carts have stopped, and nobody out there is hungry for it.
They have a wall, a well and a name. They are still sending us a share of what they used to, unasked.
Another light, and it is not yours. That is the better kind.
There is room on the list for another camp. I expect there always will be.
The packet you read held a location: the company's headquarters. It is down. Nobody has been there to answer anything for a long time.

Your record speaks for itself. Power, people, a Beacon that was heard, districts, a station in orbit. You are qualified to run this colony on your own. Only the headquarters can make it official, and it cannot do anything until it is rebuilt.

The bill is heavy: orbital goods, trade goods and a great deal of ordinary stock, delivered to the Core in any instalments. A Headquarters screen has opened beside the Data screen. Rebuild it, and the colony gets its independent charter.
The headquarters is standing again, and it has issued the colony's independent charter. You are its Independent Colony Commander now.
The charter grant is in the treasury, and your station carries the charter mark in orbit.

Nothing here changes overnight, and nobody is going anywhere: we are still here to help. But from now on you decide what comes next. The headquarters will build new districts, station expansions, wider roads and territory equipment, each dearer than the last. The first one is free.
Yours now. Go on.

mail.subject: Lights on
body: The grid is holding. It is not much, but it is ours.
Scrap next. Everything we build is paid for in it.

mail.subject: A convoy at the gate
body: Traders pass on a schedule. They pay for surplus and they sell what we cannot make.
Set your terms before they arrive. They will not wait.

mail.subject: Ten filled
body: Ten requisitions filled. The courier has stopped checking the count before he signs.
He left a note from the far end this time. It says the water arrived the day their tanks ran dry. It is pinned up in the stores.

mail.subject: A second crew
body: The second crew is working. Two jobs at once, each still taken in the order you set.
The foremen argue about everything except one rule: nobody starts what the stores cannot pay for.

mail.subject: Another way to run it
body: One of our lines is running a different recipe from the one it was built with. The manuals had more in them than we were using.
More recipes open as the hub and the districts grow. Changing one idles the line while it retools, so choose with the stores in mind.

mail.subject: Concentrated power
body: The first power cell came off the line today. Dense, quiet, and worth more than the rest of the cache together.
The transmitter is within reach.

mail.subject: The array rests
body: The array has said what it had to say. It no longer burns power cells, only enough power to stay lit.
The cells are ours again. There will be no shortage of uses.

mail.subject: The first cart
body: The first cart went out this morning. One will go every tick until you say otherwise.
Now and then they will appeal for one thing in a hurry. Answering is worth it, and ignoring it costs nothing but the chance.

mail.subject: The furnace camp
body: Those are furnace people you are feeding. Some of them were mine once.
They will pay you in work. Do not call it charity where they can hear.

mail.subject: The valley families
body: The families in the valley have water and food now. I went to see. They are planting already.
Some will walk in to work for you each morning. Let them go home at night.

mail.subject: The junction
body: You took on the junction. Good. Track, sidings, and a stationmaster who never stopped keeping the timetable.
Keep it supplied and the roads carry more. Let it go short and the extra room goes with it, so do not build on all of it.

mail.subject: They asked, we answered
body: The camp asked for one thing and got all of it the same day. They have put in double turns for us since.
They did not have to. I think that is the point they are making.

mail.subject: You are not alone
body: Every order you fill is heard further than you think.
There are others like you. In time, you may meet them.

mail.subject: A seat at the table
body: You have earned a name in the foundries. That does not happen often.
There will be work for you, if you want it.

mail.subject: Seeds for the road
body: The valley remembers its friends.
Come and see what grows when it is tended properly.

mail.subject: Preferred routing
body: Your crates arrive on time and in one piece. We notice.
Consider yourself on our short list.

mail.subject: Payload ready
body: The payload is complete and the staging platform has stood down. The catapult is waiting for your word, and a name for the station.

mail.subject: Samples
body: The dropship brought back something the colony has never had. The orbital foundry can work it, two kinds at a time.
Whatever it makes may be worth bringing back down. The colony's buildings were laid out to grow taller than they are.
